observed_vs_expected: The expectation that best_target_score would increase under the quarter-wave hypothesis was met transiently but ultimately contradicted by long-term behavior. Scores rose sharply from 0.9608361113958903 (round 1) to 0.9822912624963696 (round 3), then plateaued and oscillated. The current round 8 score of 0.9829661730320621 shows a NEGATIVE DEVIATION of ~0.00059 from the historical peak of 0.9835573025853339 (round 6). Conversely, expectations for structural stability were fully met: tightest_margin remained positive at 0.9515601240874388 across all rounds, and valid_candidates held steady at 9, confirming designs remained fully realizable within bounds.
deviation_mechanism: The initial score ascent reflects the optimizer locating thicknesses that roughly satisfy quarter-wave phase accumulation near the target 550 nm wavelength. As optimization progressed, the solver systematically broke quarter-wave symmetry to minimize broadband error and maximize target coupling. Candidate 1 illustrates this extreme adaptation: layer 0 contracted from initialization to 45.82884673254962 nm, while layer 23 expanded to 150.05806245688382 nm, altering the optical path ratio to satisfy precise interference conditions. With a 12-pair (24-layer) stack, the system possesses sufficient degrees of freedom to approach the analytical transmission/reflection limit for the given material indices. Once phase-matching and impedance matching are nearly optimized, further thickness adjustments produce spectral perturbations smaller than the scoring function's resolution, causing performance saturation. The intermittent drops (round 4: 0.7378606694308509; round 7: 0.939740565450821) represent transient stochastic excursions into non-resonant phase configurations before gradient correction restored high-fidelity alignments.
